Kingston.method_notes: Kingston (admissions run by Achieving for Children) uses a straight-line measurement in metres from a grid reference point within the home property supplied by Ordnance Survey (the 'seed point') to the closest named school gate set out in the school's admission arrangements, calculated by the council's GIS; only GIS distances are used. Community school arrangements: main school gate, or nearest gate where more than one (nearest pedestrian gate used by the year group). Community oversubscription order: looked-after children, siblings, exceptional need, staff children, distance. No nodal points or catchment areas. Some faith/academy schools use different end points (central point of site, specific gates) or faith/parish/designated-area criteria.

Lambeth.method_notes: Lambeth community schools (LA as admission authority): distance is a straight line measured by a computerised mapping system from a point at the home address identified via the Local Land and Property Gazetteer (LLPG) to a central point in the school's grounds as profiled in the software. Closest-first tie-breaker; equal distances resolved by random allocation (Synergy). Exceptions: Henry Cavendish (two sites) uses nodal points (Balham: Hydethorpe Road; Streatham: Dingley Lane); Sudbourne has a different proximity point (measured from the Mandrell Road site per brochure); Kingswood measured to the upper site. Own-admission-authority schools vary: Christ Church Streatham (pedestrian gate), St Leonard's (pupil gate), St Luke's (Linton Grove entrance), Corpus Christi (main reception entrance), Dunraven (North Site entrance), Rosendale (central point as council). Walking routes are used by Iqra (walking distance), Orchard (safest walking route) and Julian's (shortest walking route). All 'last distance' columns in the community allocation tables are headed 'Last distance - straight line (metres)'. Sources: Determined 2026-27 Lambeth school admissions arrangements (criterion 5, p.7-8) and the 2026-27 primary admissions brochure.

Richmond.method_notes: Council (Achieving for Children) measures home-to-school distance in metres as the shortest route by road and/or maintained footpath using the School Admissions GIS and Ordnance Survey data. Start: OS address/seed point within the property (route joins nearest road centre; all flats in a block share one point). End: nearest named (pedestrian) school gate or nodal point designated in the school's admission arrangements. Excludes routes through car parks, parks, cemeteries, private paths etc.; council says these are not promoted as actual walking routes. Exceptions per council guide (2026 and 2027 entry): Deer Park, St Elizabeth's Catholic Primary, Thomson House and Twickenham Primary Academy measure in a straight line from the seed point to school-designated gate(s). Faith schools (VA/Catholic academies) allocate many places by faith/parish criteria first. Sources: Richmond primary guide 2027 entry (Sep 2026) and 2026 entry; Admission arrangements for Richmond community schools 2027/28.
